key_insight: Train reward models directly in the diffusion model's latent space (diffusion-native) instead of relying on expensive pixel-space VLM rewards—this reduces compute/memory costs and removes the domain mismatch between reward and generator.
problem_solved: Addresses the high computational/memory cost and domain mismatch that arise when using pixel-space Vision–Language Model (VLM) rewards to steer latent diffusion and flow‑matching generators during preference optimization.
method: Define and train a reward model that operates in the generator's latent space (latent reward modeling) so rewards align with the diffusion representation.
Use preference-driven objectives (e.g., pairwise comparisons or contrastive signals) adapted to latent embeddings to learn discriminative, robust rewards.
Integrate the latent reward into preference optimization loops for diffusion and flow‑matching models to guide generation with lower overhead and tighter alignment.
impact: Makes alignment and preference optimization for diffusion/flow models more computationally efficient and semantically consistent, enabling faster iteration and deployment of aligned generative models without heavy VLM dependencies.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: VLM pixel-reward (heavy compute, domain gap) vs. diffusion-native latent reward (lightweight, aligned).

Embedding alignment visualization (e.g., t-SNE) showing closer alignment between generator latents and learned latent rewards vs. pixel-reward signals.
paper_title: Beyond VLM-Based Rewards: Diffusion-Native Latent Reward Modeling
paper_authors: Gongye Liu, Bo Yang, Yida Zhi, Zhizhou Zhong, Lei Ke
